user.title: Step 1 of 2: connect to Zonneburen
user.description: Open the Zonneburen web app, go to **My hub** and create a pairing code. Enter that code here.

data_description.server: Leave this as is, unless your neighbourhood has its own web app.
data_description.code: The code from the web app. Upper or lower case doesn't matter.

sensoren.title: Step 2 of 2: your sensors
sensoren.description:
Connected as **{adres}**.

Pick the sensors Home Assistant already knows about your home. Only **Grid** is required; the others make the charts in the web app more complete. You can always change this later with **Configure**.

data.wijk_automatisch: Join automatically when the neighbourhood has a surplus
data.bediening: Allow control from the web app

data_description.net: The power (W) from your smart meter. Should be positive when you import and negative when you export.
data_description.net_omdraaien: Tick this if your meter does it the other way round: positive when exporting.
data_description.zon: The power your solar panels produce right now.
data_description.batterij: The power of your home battery. Should be positive when discharging.
data_description.batterij_omdraaien: Tick this if your battery reports positive while charging.
data_description.soc: How full the battery is, in percent.
data_description.verbruik: What your whole house uses right now.
data_description.wijk_automatisch: When the neighbourhood has power to spare, Home Assistant switches on your chosen devices (water heater, EV charger) by itself. Off: you get a notification to confirm first.
data_description.bediening: Lets you switch devices in Home Assistant on and off from the web app.

error.code_onbekend: This code is unknown or expired. Create a new one in the web app.
error.niet_toegestaan: The server refuses this pairing. Ask your neighbourhood board for help.
error.te_vaak: Too many attempts. Try again in fifteen minutes.
error.niet_bereikbaar: The web app cannot be reached. Check the address and your internet connection.
error.geen_https: The address must start with https://.

energieplan.name: Energy plan (control your home battery)
energieplan.description: First set **Energy plan** to **Control** in the web app. Then choose here how Home Assistant drives your battery.

data.ems_vermogen: Entity that sets the battery power
data.ems_netdoel: This entity is a grid target

data_description.ems_aan: Main switch. You can also turn this on and off later with the Carry out energy plan switch.
data_description.ems_vermogen: A number entity (W) from your battery integration, such as the charge/discharge power. Positive means discharging.
data_description.ems_netdoel: Tick this if the entity sets the desired power on the grid rather than the battery power, like the grid setpoint of a Victron ESS.
data_description.ems_laden_positief: Tick this if the entity uses a positive number for charging.
data_description.ems_modus: Only needed if your battery must first be put in a mode for external control.
data_description.ems_modus_sturen: Exactly as the option is named in the list, for example Remote control. Leave empty if not needed.
data_description.ems_modus_terug: The mode in which the battery manages itself again, for example Self consumption.
data_description.ems_max_laad_w: In watts. Empty or 0: the maximum from the plan.
data_description.ems_max_ontlaad_w: In watts. Empty or 0: the maximum from the plan.
data_description.ems_zekering_a: In amps. The battery charges less hard as soon as a phase gets close to this value.
